item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next?

AI Rout Turns Gold Into Source Of Cash: What Comes Next? 2 min read

QQQ NEM B AEM Gold fell to a 14-month low on Friday as a rout in technology shares prompted investors to sell bullion to cover losses elsewhere. The metal slid alongside falling Treasury yields and the US dollar. Spot gold fell to $3,502 an ounce- the lowest level since September 2025. In total, bullion lost 8.9% for the week, while the Invesco QQQ ETF QQQ sank 9.31% and State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:SPY) fell by 7.98%, entering correction territory Rate Hike Bets Set the Stage Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting showed that nearly all policymakers anticipated further rate increases . According to the CME FedWatch , traders currently price in an 88.6% chance of a quarter-point increase in December. “The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses,” David Meger , director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, told Reuters. Ole Hansen , head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, wrote that bullion “has become a source of cash for investors facing mounting losses elsewhere,” Mining.com reported. In a market commentary, former Bridgewater economist Bob Elliott said pro-growth pricing “remains quite elevated” and warned the selloff could become “more self-reinforcing to the downside.” Once downturns start, he wrote, they typically require “both much cheaper pricing and some sort of policy support to get to the bottom, neither of which we are at yet.” Interestingly, there was little sign of a broad exit from gold funds. Holdings in gold ETFs tracked by Bloomberg were little changed over the preceding month despite a roughly 10% drop in bullion, Hansen said. Mining shares were less resilient, since their leverage to gold price works both ways. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (NYSE:GDX) closed the week 14.80% below the previous Friday’s close. The largest names in the sector, Newmont NEM , Barrick Mining B and Agnico Eagle Mines AEM lost 15.03%, 15.19% and 13.64%, respectively. Technical Outlook Gold’s daily chart shows the magnitude of the post-summer carnage. After peaking in August and briefly moving above the 200-day moving average, bullion reversed course and fell by over 25%.

Gold, daily chart, Source: TradingView Zooming out, the next key support area is the Q2-Q3 2025 price range. For much of that time, price remained in a tight accumulation between $3,200 and $3,450. Thus, price could easily fall further, test that range, and wait for the next catalyst to move it either way.

item.content:encoded:
News / U.Today / XRP Ledger Loses 60% of Users

XRP Ledger Loses 60% of Users 1 min read

XRPUSD XRP Ledger's network activity has dropped sharply, losing around 60% of the users it had yesterday. The decline comes amid a serious price correction and increased pressure on the cryptocurrency market. Selling pressure remains high, and the declining number of users is not helping the price. Fuel for the correction XRPScan's data showed 250,000 users 24 hours ago, while today's reading shows barely 92,000 users. While the drop is significant, it should not be considered critical on its own. The decline partly reflects a regular weekend slowdown, when traders are generally less active, but it comes alongside the price correction and broader selling pressure.

BITSTAMP:XRPUSDT Chart by TradingView"> The highest point for this metric in November was 300,000, with a monthly average of approximately 200,000 active users. The number of users is a critical metric for the network's health, and a decline toward 100,000 often comes before bullish sentiment among investors. The current drop does not guarantee that sentiment will turn, especially as the price remains under pressure. Price action remains weak Apart from the negative on-chain trend, XRP's price performance has also been weak. The price lost roughly 5% from its November 19 close and even fell below the $0.90 price level, which was expected to serve as a foundation for recovery. XRP was around $0.915 on November 22 after closing at $0.9604 three days earlier. The trend remains bearish, and the decline could become significantly worse. Few expected a surge in market liquidations so soon, as Bitcoin fell below the $60,000 price level. XRP and other altcoins followed the broader market trend and suffered serious losses. Interest in the network appears to be weakening as the price correction continues, so this drop in activity is not helping XRP's recovery. A potential recovery above $0.9 could be the key to a quick rebound. However, the overall trend remains bearish and is unlikely to change unless significant market events occur.
